verifications.note:
Verified on candidate sha256:9331e9d13e0ffa55f35ebc25ecdf9b60e159876dc2470fe56e9241a40fea124f (source cf3446e4, 539 files). I recomputed it in a disposable clone at cf3446e4 and at HEAD 4053630c, and ran it against disposable PostgreSQL 16 clusters with LANG unset (SQL_ASCII) and LANG=C.UTF-8 (UTF8).
(1) My round-7 repro, zz-sec-r7-probe.test.ts, rerun unchanged, now passes 14/14 in both runs (in round 7: 12 pass, 2 fail):
- B1: charter create with a Content-Length body holding ED A0 80, FF or C3 now gets 400 validation.json at pointer '' (it was 500 internal). There is no charter and no audit row. Control 0x41 still gives 201.
- B2: unauthenticated, over a real socket: 400 validation.json as problem+json (it was a 500). Control: 401.
- B3: chunked and authenticated: 400 (it was 201 with Synthetic\uFFFD text stored and audited). Nothing is stored, and no U+FFFD appears in charter or audit_event.changes.
(2) Code. server.ts registers addContentTypeParser('application/json', { parseAs: 'buffer' }, createJsonBodyParser(app.getDefaultJsonParser('error','error'))).
- Fastify 5.6.1 addContentTypeParser fills a missing bodyLimit with the server bodyLimit (contentTypeParser.js:344), so the 1 MiB limit still applies. With asBuffer, rawBody counts raw chunk.length (:246), so the Content-Length comparison is on raw bytes.
- decodeUtf8Body uses a fresh TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true }) and strips exactly one U+FEFF. A second leading U+FEFF is refused as validation.json.
- The text then goes to Fastify's own defaultJsonParser (secure-json-parse with protoAction and constructorAction 'error'; FST_ERR_CTP_EMPTY_JSON_BODY / INVALID_JSON_BODY), so prototype-poisoning protection and the error codes are unchanged.
- mapError additionally maps FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_CONTENT_LENGTH to 400 validation.malformed_request, so no framing error reaches the 500 path.
- The evidence octet-stream parser is untouched: the stream is handed to the handler, and the size limit is enforced while streaming.
- parseQueryString (routerOptions.querystringParser) keeps the null-prototype shape and marks undecodable components through a WeakMap. Nothing reassigns request.query, and there is no validatorCompiler that could replace it, so the mark survives until the preHandler check. That check runs after authentication and CSRF, and the OIDC callback (invalidCharacters: 'route') keeps its 302.
(3) Adversarial probe zz-sec-r8-probe.test.ts, both runs:
- R1: ten ill-formed classes, in both framings, all give 400 validation.json with nothing stored and no error log: overlong C0 AF and E0 80 AF; F4 90 80 80; the 5-byte F8; a lone 80; truncated E2 82, mid-body and trailing; CESU low ED B0 80; Latin-1 E9.
- R2: one BOM gives 201 with the exact text. Two BOMs, BOM+FF, a BOM alone, and UTF-16LE/BE bodies give 400. A U+FEFF inside a string is kept verbatim.
- R3: charset=iso-8859-1 or utf-16le never switches the decoder (400). Other +json types give 400 validation.content_type.
- R4: __proto__ (plain and \u-escaped) and constructor.prototype give 400 validation.json, with no pollution.
- R5: 349,571 characters = 1,048,629 bytes gives 400 body_too_large in both framings.
- R7: query pointers /query/q, /query, /query/a~0b~1c; a stray % gives 400; '+' and emoji decode; 401 precedes; an unmatched route gives 404; no error log.
- R8: an X-File-Name refusal never precedes authorization: a non-editor gets 403.
- R9: chunked, no session: 400.
- R10: no U+FFFD in charter, audit_event or evidence_content.file_name.
(4) The candidate's own invalid-utf8.test.ts (14 tests) and request-encoding unit tests (18) pass on Node 22 and 24 and in both locales. Cookies and headers stay byte-faithful (Latin-1); the round-7 C1/C2 probes still pass.
The one residual this round found has a different root cause: the evidence upload route accepts text/plain and application/json bodies that its contract does not declare, and the store iterates whatever body it receives. It predates BE13 (same behaviour at 90439483) and is raised separately as F-DG2-320 (Low). This finding's scope and stated remedy, JSON bodies and query strings decoded strictly with a declared 400 in every framing, are fully fixed.
